articles.title: Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. is unsure if he'll play Week 1 if a new deal isn't in place
articles.summary: Joey Porter Jr.'s balky back felt good enough to return to practice for the Pittsburgh Steelers on Tuesday.  The fourth-year cornerback didn't commit to play...
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH (AP) — Joey Porter Jr.'s balky back felt good enough to return to practice for the Pittsburgh Steelers on Tuesday.

At the moment, his health appears to be the least of his concerns.

The fourth-year cornerback didn't commit to playing in Pittsburgh's season opener against Atlanta on Sept. 13 if he and the team can't come to terms on a new contract.

"I don't know," Porter said. "I've got to talk to (the front office) and my agents about that one."

The 26-year-old is entering the final season of the rookie contract he signed after being selected with the first pick of the second round in 2023. He said during minicamp in June that he believes he's one of the best defensive backs in the league and is confident that he'll be compensated that way.

Three months later, Porter has yet to put pen to paper.

While general manager Omar Khan said Monday he wants Porter — the son of former Steelers linebacker and coach Joey Porter Sr. — to be in Pittsburgh for the entirety of his career, it doesn't feel as if the two sides are particularly close.

Porter, who hasn't allowed a touchdown pass while being the primary defender since his rookie season, essentially grew up in the Steelers locker room. His ties to the organization are deep, which has made the process of separating the business side of things difficult.

"It's been tough, I'm not going to lie, and it's my first go-around with this," Porter said. "But I mean, it's been also great because I have all my guys with me, all the coaches and players really are on my side."

Veteran defensive back Jalen Ramsey recently said it was time for the Steelers to pay Porter, though first-year coach Mike McCarthy described the two sides as at an impasse.

Asked if he hopes something gets done with the opener less than two weeks away, Porter shrugged.

"I could hope and think all day, but it's really, it's up to (the front office) and what they want to do with this team," he said. "So all I can do is just show up every day to work and be prepared."

Pittsburgh has already handed out new deals to several other members of the 2023 draft class, including linebacker Nick Herbig and tight end Darnell Washington . Porter said he's happy for his teammates and has no issue with the team taking care of them.

"Those are my guys," Porter said. "So I was ecstatic that they got paid."

The Steelers have a long-held policy of not negotiating once the regular season begins, meaning there is a firm deadline in place.

It's not unusual for Pittsburgh to put things together at the last minute. Star outside linebacker T.J. Watt agreed to terms less than 72 hours before the opening kickoff in Week 1 of the 2021 season.

"Things carry out a long time," Porter said. "I know T.J. went through this. Cam Heyward went through this as well. So I never really had a clock on it. If it gets done, it gets done. If it don't, it don't."

Heyward said his advice to Porter was "don't take it personal, but you will." Though the seven-time Pro Bowler added he is not worried about the contract being an issue whenever Porter takes the field.

"I think every player in there says Joey's got to do what's best for him and Joey's got to be ready for Week 1, and hopefully we can celebrate a new contract for him," Heyward said.

Though he's been limited by a back issue that cropped up during a mobility test when the team reported to training camp in late July, Porter has been in the classroom studying up on first-year defensive coordinator Patrick Graham's approach.

Porter stressed the injury was the sole reason for his absence during camp, and Heyward believes whenever Porter gets out there he'll be ready to continue on the trajectory that's made him one of the better man-to-man defenders in the league.

"We're expecting him to be the Joey of usual," Heyward said. "I don't think there's going to be a drop-off. I think we've all got to be ready to welcome him back."

articles.title: No. 2 Oregon turns to a goal-setting method used by Shohei Ohtani as it chases a national title
articles.summary: When a young Shohei Ohtani was envisioning his future in baseball, he turned to a goal-setting tool developed by a Japanese track coach.  The Harada Method f...
articles.body:
EUGENE, Ore. (AP) — When a young Shohei Ohtani was envisioning his future in baseball, he turned to a goal-setting tool developed by a Japanese track coach.

The Harada Method for setting and achieving goals, once used by Ohtani to manifest a major league career, has now been adopted in football by No. 2 Oregon .

The idea is that there's one ultimate goal, with eight supporting pillars as a path and actionable items beneath each pillar. Coach Dan Lanning introduced the tool to players at a team retreat this summer.

"It just lays out our format of things that we want to do this year. Coach Lanning has always been a big write things out on his mirror, write things out on the board, and really speak into existence. And this year, I've done the same thing," said quarterback Dante Moore, who will start for the Ducks again this year after he opted out of declaring for the NFL draft.

The Ducks have lofty goals after they reached the College Football Playoff in each of the past two seasons but fell short of a national title.

Last season, Oregon went 13-2, with both losses coming to Fernando Mendoza and national champion Indiana. The Ducks enter this season with the highest preseason ranking in program history.

"It started a little bit with our leadership group when we did our leadership retreat; went through it, kind of built out some of our vision boards," Lanning said. "Some of our players have done the same thing individually. But yeah, kind of grew from there."

The message resonated for many of the Ducks.

"The Harada method definitely helps you hone in on little goals before getting to that big goal, and if you can't do those little goals, like you just can't expect that big goal, and that's been the main thing we've been preaching," receiver Evan Stewart said.

Oregon brings a loaded offense into the season, led by Moore, who threw for 3,565 yards and 30 touchdowns last year. Stewart is back after missing last season with a torn patellar tendon, and he'll be joined by standout receiver Dakorian Moore. The defensive line is also a strength, with Matayo Uiagalelei, Bear Alexander and A'Mauri Washington all returning after eschewing the NFL draft.

Alexander posted his square Harada board on Instagram . In the center box was his central goal: becoming a first-round draft pick. Among his eight pillars in boxes surrounding that goal were faith, discipline, character and health. The actionable items beneath character included "being kind" and "giving back."

Lanning said he and Cory Shaffer, a mental performance consultant for the Ducks, were interested in the Harada Method before it became a tool for the players.

The method was developed by Takashi Harada, a junior high track coach who aimed to inspire underperforming athletes through discipline and self-reliance. While originally used in sports, it has been adapted to business, too.

"It's something that I was kind of studying before, and then Cory and I both actually sent it to each other. So, it kind of worked out and was like, OK, this might be something we want to surround some of our thought processes," Lanning said. "It started a little bit with our leadership group. We did our leadership retreat, went through it, kind of built out some of our vision boards, and some of our players have done the same thing individually."

"Ohtani is probably going to be the greatest baseball player of all time, I mean, at the end of the day, what he's done," Moore said. "But yeah, we're just trying to learn from the greats and make sure we be that team this year."

articles.title: Eagles Make Jonathan Greenard Decision as Howie Roseman Reveals Expectations for His Return
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles have made an encouraging decision regarding Jonathan Greenard ahead of their Week 1 matchup with the Washington Commanders. Philadelp...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have made an encouraging decision regarding Jonathan Greenard ahead of their Week 1 matchup with the Washington Commanders . Philadelphia did not place the veteran edge rusher on the physically unable to perform list to begin the regular season. Among other things, the decision suggests a green light about Greenard's recovery from a pec strain.

Greenard was placed on the PUP list before training camp and has not practiced with the Eagles this summer. Consequently, many initially raised questions about whether he would be available for the start of the regular season. However, general manager Howie Roseman offered a more encouraging outlook while discussing the decision to keep Greenard on the active roster.

Eagles Expect Greenard Back Sooner Rather Than Later

Roseman stopped short of p roviding a specific return date, but his comments suggested the Eagles believe Greenard will not be sidelined for an extended period. NFL insider John Clark shared Roseman's explainer on the situation via his X account.

"Us not having him on PUP and missing time here shows that we anticipate him playing sooner rather than later. What that timetable is, again, we'll keep close to the vest. The guy's a tremendous football player. He's got a tremendous ability to affect the quarterback. He's going to come back in tremendous shape. I think that you saw the D-Line's obviously a position of emphasis for us always. The guy fits what we do. Yeah, there'll be some things that will be a little bit different and we'll get him up to speed, but we expect him to have a high impact on this team this season for all accounts of what he's done and how he works and how he leads, he's as advertised. We're excited to have him."

The Eagles' decision to keep Greenard on the 53-man roster means they expect him to contribute relatively soon. However, Philadelphia has not confirmed whether that means Week 1 against Washington.

The team is taking a cautious approach with the injury. Greenard's absence throughout training camp means he will need time to regain his football conditioning before returning to game action.

Considering that the Eagles made a significant investment in Greenard this offseason, there's little surprise about the rationale for maintaining their big-money acquisition. Philadelphia acquired Greenard and Minnesota's 2026 seventh-round pick in exchange for a 2026 third-round pick and a 2027 third-rounder.

The Eagles signed Greenard to a four-year, $100 million extension that includes $50 million fully guaranteed, underlining the organization's belief in his ability to impact the defense. Yet, there's no denying that Greenard has already demonstrated his immense ability during his NFL career.

The former Florida standout entered the league as a third-round pick by the Houston Texans in 2020. After showing steady development, he broke out with 12.5 sacks in 15 games during the 2023 season. He then joined the Vikings in free agency and produced 12 sacks during his first season in Minnesota. Greenard also forced four fumbles during his 2024 Pro Bowl season.

His 2025 campaign was interrupted by a season-ending injury after 12 games as he finished that season with 38 tackles and three sacks. But by the middle of 2025, Greenard had already built a career history that reinforced the Eagles' confidence in their investment despite his current absence.

articles.title: Eagles expect Jonathan Greenard to return sooner rather than later
articles.summary: Howie Roseman expects Jonathan Greenard back soon and believes he will make a major 2026 impact
articles.body:
Jonathan Greenard missed valuable practice time while learning the Philadelphia Eagles' defense, but the organization expects its veteran edge rusher to return sooner rather than later. The Athletic's Brooks Kubena asked general manager Howie Roseman how quickly Greenard could get up to speed after defensive coordinator Vic Fangio acknowledged that his role would include some new coverage responsibilities.

"Us not having him on PUP and missing time here shows that we anticipate him playing sooner rather than later," Roseman said. "What that timetable is, again, we'll keep close to the vest."

Placing Greenard on the physically unable to perform list would have required him to miss at least the opening four games. Keeping him on the active roster leaves open the possibility of an earlier return. Philadelphia acquired Greenard during the draft, sending third-round selections in 2026 and 2027 to Minnesota for the veteran and a seventh-round pick. He is expected to become a central piece of a rotation that includes Nolan Smith, Jalyx Hunt, A.J. Epenesa and Arnold Ebiketie.

"The guy's a tremendous football player," Roseman said. "He's got a tremendous ability to affect the quarterback."

Greenard must learn some responsibilities that differ from those in his previous assignments, but his primary job will remain pressuring quarterbacks and strengthening a defensive front that the Eagles consistently prioritize.

Roseman also praised Greenard's conditioning, leadership and approach during his rehabilitation.

"We expect him to have a high impact on this team this season," Roseman said. "For all accounts of what he's done and how he works and how he leads, he's as advertised."

articles.title: Detroit Lions Lose Promising Rookie to Patriots
articles.summary: Former Detroit Lions rookie linebacker Erick Hunter has signed with the New England Patriots' 53-man active roster after being waived by Detroit during final...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions knew some of their difficult roster decisions could eventually benefit another NFL team.

That has now happened with rookie linebacker Erick Hunter .

The New England Patriots officially announced Tuesday that they have signed Hunter to their 53-man active roster , ending any possibility of the Lions bringing the promising undrafted rookie back to their practice squad.

NFL reporter Aaron Wilson first reported the move Tuesday afternoon:

"Erick Hunter signed to the active roster today with the New England Patriots per a league source."

For Detroit, this is not a devastating roster loss. Hunter was waived Sunday and did not make the Lions' initial practice squad.

Hunter arrived in Detroit as an undrafted free agent out of Morgan State, where he developed into one of the most productive linebackers at the FCS level.

The 6-foot-2, 224-pound linebacker finished his college career with 298 tackles, 35 tackles for loss, 10.5 sacks, seven forced fumbles and three interceptions. As a senior in 2025, Hunter piled up 102 tackles, 14 tackles for loss and four sacks while earning First-Team All-MEAC honors.

NFL.com ranked Hunter as the fifth-best undrafted linebacker available following the 2026 NFL Draft, and Detroit quickly added him to its rookie class.

He did not disappear once training camp started.

During an August scrimmage, Hunter intercepted Jared Goff in the end zone while covering Sam LaPorta, one of several plays that helped him emerge as an intriguing developmental prospect. Detroit's own Tim Twentyman specifically identified Hunter as a player to watch during the preseason because of his length and playmaking ability.

That performance put Hunter firmly into what became a crowded battle for Detroit's final linebacker positions.

We previously detailed the competition Hunter faced for a roster spot , particularly because special-teams value was going to play such a significant role in determining the final spots.

Ultimately, Detroit kept six linebackers: Jack Campbell, Derrick Barnes, Devin White, Malcolm Rodriguez, Trevor Nowaske and rookie Jimmy Rolder.

Hunter joined Joe Bachie, Troy Reeder and Amen Ogbongbemiga among the linebackers who did not survive the final cut.

Detroit officially waived Hunter following its 25-16 preseason victory over Indianapolis .

The interesting part came the following day.

Hunter cleared waivers, meaning all 31 other teams initially passed on the opportunity to claim his rookie contract. That appeared to leave the door open for a Detroit reunion, something we noted when every waived Lions player cleared the waiver wire .

Instead, New England gave Hunter something Detroit could not: an immediate place on the active roster.

That's difficult for a young player to turn down.

A Good Opportunity for Hunter, a Small Loss for Detroit

There is a distinction worth making here.

The Lions did not lose a starting linebacker or someone they had designated for their practice squad. They made the decision that Hunter was outside their top 53 and subsequently filled their practice squad with other players.

Still, losing him removes an intriguing developmental option.

Hunter has NFL athleticism, significant college production and enough special-teams ability to potentially carve out a role while he develops defensively. At 23 years old, there was plenty of reason for Detroit to remain interested in seeing where his game could go.

For Hunter, going from undrafted rookie to an NFL active roster before Week 1 represents a pretty good outcome.

For the Lions, it is another reminder of what Dan Campbell said before final cuts: when a roster becomes deep enough, eventually you're going to release players who can help somebody else.

Erick Hunter didn't have to wait long to prove the point.

articles.title: Manchester City sign Everton's Iliman Ndiaye for $88 million after Cody Gakpo move fails
articles.summary: Manchester City have completed the $87.9 million signing of Iliman Ndiaye from Everton, with the Blues reigniting their interest in the Senegal international...
articles.body:
Manchester City have wrapped up the £65 million ($87.9 million) acquisition of Everton forward Iliman Ndiaye.

The Blues will pay an initial £60 million ($81.1 million) for the 26-year-old, with a further £5 million ($6.8 million) available through add-ons. City were eager to bring in a wide forward following the departure of Omar Marmoush to Tottenham Hotspur on an initial loan deal, with a £60 million obligation to make the transfer permanent next summer.

Ndiaye had been identified by the Blues earlier this summer as a potential replacement, with City seeking someone comfortable operating from wide positions but also capable of playing centrally to ease some of the attacking burden on Erling Haaland, as per the Manchester Evening News .

Ndiaye has found the net 17 times for Everton since making the move to Merseyside from Marseille in 2024. He featured in each of the Toffees' opening three fixtures of the campaign but has now linked up with City and could make his debut for the Blues in Saturday's home game against Coventry City.

The Senegal international had also attracted interest from Tottenham, who had been hoping to finalize a deal that would have seen former Everton forward Richarlison return to the Hill Dickinson Stadium. However, an agreement could not be reached, prompting City to reignite their pursuit of Ndiaye after the Blues' hopes of securing Liverpool's Cody Gakpo had fallen through.

City had initiated discussions with Liverpool regarding a potential £80 million ($108.1 million) transfer for the Netherlands international, an agreement the Anfield club were prepared to approve on the condition they could secure a replacement. However, Andoni Iraola's team have been frustrated in their efforts to bolster the squad, and Gakpo's proposed Etihad move was called off, leading City to revive their pursuit of Ndiaye.

Upon completing his move to the club, Ndiaye said: "It's easy to make the decision about whether you want to be at Manchester City or not. You can see the recent history; you want to be part of that project. They talked to me about where we could go, what we could achieve with me in the team, and I was interested from the beginning. There was nothing else that I wanted other than joining Manchester City.

"It's an unbelievable moment. I've worked so hard to get to this point and I'm super excited and really grateful for this opportunity. Obviously, you want to be part of this new project. Obviously, I've seen recently what they've been doing, and I feel like I will fit right in it. I'm super excited to start."

City Sporting Director Hugo Viana commented: "Iliman is a very talented footballer. He's had to work incredibly hard to reach this level and in my first conversation with him it was immediately obvious how grounded he is and the determination he has to be the best player he can be.

"I've no doubt City fans will get a thrill seeing him in action for us. We know this club develops players. We make a commitment to every single player we sign that we will make them better footballers.

"I am really excited to see the level Iliman can reach in the years ahead because I know for sure working with Enzo and his staff is going to ensure he becomes a top-class Premier League player."

Golden State star Stephen Curry recently (August 29) became eligible to sign a max contract extension; however, the Davidson product has yet to put pen to paper. articles.title: Sprinters vs. long-distance fantasy drafters: which one are you?
articles.summary: As fantasy draft season heats up, it's important to understand what kind of drafter you are: a sprinter, or a long-distance drafter. Here's why.
articles.body:
As fantasy draft season heats up, it's important to understand what kind of drafter you are: a sprinter or a long-distance drafter. Here's why.

Sprinters excel in the early rounds. They've carefully thought through their top target with their opening pick, and maybe a backup option or two just in case. They've considered whether they might take an RB or WR in the second round, or maybe even an uber-elite QB or TE. Some of the best sprinters have mapped out a game plan that takes them into the fourth or even the fifth round.

Then things start getting tougher for sprinters. The RB "dead zone" (which actually coincides with the lesser-discussed WR dead zone) generates more choices. Sprinters are straight-line runners. They don't want a lot of choices. They want the clarity of the early rounds replicated in the later rounds. But that's not how drafts work.

Long-distance drafters approach this process differently. They prepare for all 16, 18, or however many rounds the draft is. Perhaps they don't know their top targets for each round. But they do know that the attention they pay with their first pick should match the attention they pay with their 16th pick. Bargains can be found everywhere.

Sprinters can't wait to finish. Long-distance drafters can't wait to pick. Decide which one you are, and more importantly, which one you want to be.

articles.title: Bills Receive Encouraging Injury Update on Keon Coleman Two Days After Final Roster Cuts
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills received a great injury update on wide receiver Keon Coleman a few days after final roster cuts. The post Bills Receive Encouraging Injury...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills returned to practice on Tuesday with their 53-man roster and practice squad, and they got some exciting news.

Wide receiver Keon Coleman was spotted practicing. Coleman hasn't been on the field since he suffered a foot/toe injury in the first Bills preseason game against the Carolina Panthers at Highmark Stadium on Aug 15.

With less than two weeks until the Bills take on the Houston Texans on Sept. 13 at 1 p.m. ET at Reliant Stadium, it appears Coleman is back on track to play.

Coleman is heading into a make-or-break season. He is entering his third season, and the first two have been a roller coaster. Coleman recorded 29 receptions for 556 yards and four scores in 13 games. But he suffered a chip bone in his wrist in a Week 9 game against the Miami Dolphins, which caused him to miss four games.

The 23-year-old receiver then turned around in 2025, and it didn't get much better. He appeared in 13 games, starting six, recording 38 receptions for 404 yards and four scores.

Former head coach Sean McDermott placed Coleman as a healthy scratch for a few games. However, now that Joe Brady is the head coach, it seems like Coleman is ready for another chance.

"I told Keon when I got hired, the best thing that happened to Keon Coleman was me being his head coach," Brady said in late January, via ESPN's Alaina Getzenberg. "The day he was officially introduced for his new role. "I was one of the ones that stood on the table for Keon Coleman, and I believe in Keon Coleman.

"He's going to continue to grow, but the elements that we saw in the draft process — the confidence that I have in him and his ability — and as long as he's handling what he needs to do off the field, I have no doubt that he's going to be successful on the field," Brady said.

It will be interesting to see how the Bills handle Coleman this season. If he can take a leap, then Josh Allen is going to be happy.

Bills QB Josh Allen Saw Improvement From Coleman This Offseason

Allen saw a different approach from Coleman during the offseason and into OTAs and mini camp.

"At the end of the day, the only thing I want from [Coleman] is to be the best version of himself," Allen said in May, via Bills On SI's Alex Brasky. "And I truly believe that here is the best way to do it. I've already seen a shift in his mindset this year and how hard he's been coming out to practice and working out, and so that's obviously very promising.

"But again, we don't need Keon to be any more than what Keon is. And I fully believe in him. I still do. And that'll never change."

Getting Coleman on track would be great for the Bills this season. Additionally, Buffalo needs to improve by adding young playmakers, and it would be fantastic to have one on the roster already.

articles.title: Tucker Kraft Makes Feelings Clear on Packers Future
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers tight end Tucker Kraft made it clear to the organization that he anticipates playing for the team for a long time. However, he also noted t...
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers tight end Tucker Kraft made it clear to the organization that he anticipates playing for the team for a long time. However, he also noted that negotiations have been tougher than expected as he ramps up for the season.

"It's just a game of back and forth, and my job, my responsibility is to focus on the Minnesota Vikings," Kraft told reporters.

Kraft noted that talks have been quiet of late, and his job is to focus on football and not let that impact him. He also noted that he sees this with every player and every General Manager, so he does not take personal offense to it.

Tucker Kraft Opens Up on Contract Negotiations With Green Bay Packers

However, he has made it clear that he wants to play for the team. Once the team shows that same commitment, he plans to sign with them.

"The plan for me is to stay in this organization," said Kraft. "I would love for everybody to be on the same page when it comes to that in my negotiations."

Kraft is making it clear that he feels he is one of the better tight ends in the NFL and expects to be paid in that manner, though. While he will do what it takes to stick with the team, he is entering his age 26 season.

The next time he will sign an extension will likely be at age 30, which will be a much different discussion when it comes to his value. That is why Kraft and his team are being so delicate.

"I only get one crack at getting an extension like this," Kraft admitted. "I want the best for what I can get."

Kraft added that he has given the team plenty of reasons to extend him.

"I put it all out there every single clip; checkdowns I turn into 15 and 20," said Kraft.

However, he did admit that if a deal does not get done, it will not impact his performance on the field. He is going to play for them and let the chips fall into place when they do.

"I will be on the field to play for the Green Bay Packers, regardless of any contract situation, because I love this team, and you can't replicate this locker room anywhere else in the NFL."

Still, if a deal does not get done this year, Kraft will have the ability to test the free agent market. That is where the offers can get lucrative, and it can be tough for Kraft to stay.

Packers Would Make Kraft One of the Highest Paid Tight Ends with Extension

One thing impacting Kraft is division rival Sam LaPorta. He is also does not have a contract extension. Both are young, productive, and have a chance to set the tight end market.

These two would like to top each other, and the teams want to make sure the other side is not getting a bargain in comparison. So, it brings up a bit of an interesting dynamic between the two sides.

articles.title: Browns Sign 1,000-Yard Veteran Before Week 1
articles.summary: The Browns have added a veteran back to the mix. The post Browns Sign 1,000-Yard Veteran Before Week 1 appeared first on HEAVY.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns added proven depth to their running back room by signing veteran Jaleel McLaughlin to the practice squad.

McLaughlin spent his first three NFL seasons with the Denver Broncos after signing as an undrafted free agent in 2023. The Youngstown State product appeared in 41 games for Denver, rushing for 1,093 yards and three touchdowns on 226 carries.

McLaughlin has averaged 4.8 yards per carry during his career and offers additional value as a receiver. He caught 59 passes for 263 yards and four touchdowns with the Broncos.

The 25-year-old was at his best during his first two seasons. He rushed for 410 yards while averaging 5.4 yards per carry as a rookie, then posted a career-high 496 rushing yards in 2024.

McLaughlin's role decreased last season, but he still averaged 5.1 yards on his 37 carries. Denver re-signed him to a one-year contract in March before releasing him during final roster cuts .

The Browns now get a close look at a productive player with ties to Ohio. McLaughlin finished his college career at Youngstown State and left as the NCAA's all-time leading rusher with 8,166 yards across his time with the Penguins and Notre Dame College.

Browns Add Protection Behind Quinshon Judkins

The Browns kept Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson and Raheim Sanders on their initial 53-man roster, along with fullback Michael Burton.

Judkins sits atop the depth chart after rushing for 827 yards and seven touchdowns as a rookie. However, he is returning from the fractured fibula and dislocated ankle that ended his season in December.

The second-year running back also dealt with an undisclosed nagging injury during training camp . He missed multiple practices and did not play in Cleveland's final two preseason games, although head coach Todd Monken downplayed the concern.

"I'm not worried about him overall," Monken said on August 20. "He's got something that's nagging him a little bit, so we'll be smart."

Sampson rushed for 220 yards and two touchdowns as a rookie, while Sanders emerged late last season after Judkins went down.

Browns Continue Filling Out Practice Squad

McLaughlin was one of four players the Browns added to their practice squad on Tuesday.

Cleveland also signed defensive tackles Sam Kamara and Chris Williams , along with tight end Messiah Swinson.

Kamara has appeared in 18 games for the Browns since 2022. Williams has played 44 NFL games with the Indianapolis Colts and Chicago Bears and previously spent time on Cleveland's practice squad in 2023. Swinson has had practice-squad stops with the Green Bay Packers , San Francisco 49ers and Arizona Cardinals. Those moves followed the addition of 10 practice-squad players on Monday.

Cleveland also continued reshaping its active roster , signing veteran cornerback Noah Igbinoghene and defensive end Sam Williams. The Browns placed defensive tackle Kalia Davis on injured reserve and waived preseason standout cornerback Michael Coats Jr. to make room.

articles.title: Dylan Larkin shouldn't be stripped of Red Wings' captaincy: Analyst
articles.summary: Dylan Larkin's desire to win shouldn't automatically erase his leadership status, an Athletic hockey writer said.
articles.body:
It's been almost assumed that Dylan Larkin will be stripped of the Detroit Red Wings ' captaincy this month because of his trade request at the end of last season.

The Athletic's Shayna Goldman sees another possible outcome with training camp two weeks away and a new general manager still to be named.

On Jeff Marek's podcast, "The Sheet," Goldman said Larkin's desire to win shouldn't automatically erase his leadership status or his history as the face of the franchise.

"Is Larkin part of the problem this year? Sure, but the situation just became untenable, and you want to pass forward," Goldman said on the podcast. "I almost feel like you take away the C, you're vilifying him even more."

The Red Wings went two seasons without a captain before naming Larkin the 37th captain in franchise history in 2021.

Goldman said the new GM may mend fences and keep Larkin as captain until the issue is resolved.

"I don't think any situation can't be remedied," Goldman said. "We've seen weird things happen over the years, and I think the fact that Yzerman's gone is going to open the door to this.

"Many fans are going to vilify Larkin, but there's a very simple argument of saying, the frustration was so built up from year after year, our team was not positioned to succeed.

"Yes, we could have done more down the stretch to avoid collapsing in March, but we never got the reinforcements we needed. And it wasn't just at the deadline. It was in the off-seasons too."

During the last three collapses in March and April, Larkin was injured at various times but still recorded nearly a point per game with 19 goals, 26 assists for 45 points and a -11 plus/minus rating in 50 games.

At the end of the 2025 season and after missing the playoffs for a ninth straight year, Larkin said "we didn't gain any momentum from the trade deadline," and "it would have been nice to add something and bring a little bit of a spark on the ice."

"There was no collaboration," Goldman said. "It was a frosty front office, and everyone saw it, right? Dylan Larkin gets his extension, but also (Tyler) Bertuzzi's traded, and the rug's pulled out from under them, and also you're not contending anymore. Sorry, all the progress you did, whatever.

"And then it's like they finally make a move, and it just felt like they were throwing a band-aid on a situation that needed a lot more than that, and it was work that should have been done ahead of time."

Derby County have re-signed midfielder David Ozoh from Crystal Palace for an undisclosed fee, brought Brighton defender Eiran Cashin back and added Union Saint-Gilloise forward Mohammed Fuseini on loan.

The Rams have now recruited 21-year-old Ozoh in three successive summer transfer windows, with his first two stints being season-long loans.

He has featured 47 times across two injury-interrupted stays, and done enough to earn himself a five-year deal with the Championship club.

Cashin, 24, started his career at Pride Park, helping the club win promotion back to the Championship in 2024.

He made 144 appearances for the club before departing for Brighton in January 2025 but has featured just twice for Fabian Hurzeler's side and spent last season on loan at Birmingham City and Blackburn Rovers.

Cashin's arrival was confirmed before Derby's win at Portsmouth, while the addition of 24-year-old Fuseini on a season-long loan was sealed soon after the club's first win of the Championship season.

The Ghana international moves to the English game after two years in Belgium with Union Saint-Gilloise, a club he joined in 2024 from Austrian side Sturm Gratz.

Fuseini, who started his career with Ghana's Right to Dream football academy, has also had a stint playing on loan in Denmark for Randers.

articles.title: Where Penn State lands on ESPN’s FPI ahead of Week 1
articles.summary: Penn State has mounting expectations in 2026, and those will only be ratcheted up after ESPN’s initial Football Power Index.
articles.body:
The Football Power Index is a solid indicator of how well a college football team is doing compared to the rest of the field. The rating system calculates a team's overall strength, as well as their chances of winning their conference or clinching a College Football Playoff berth.

Penn State has a favorable position on ESPN's initial index for 2026, currently sitting at No. 16 in the country ahead of Week 1, with an FPI score of 13.7. Although the method for the rankings are different, ESPN has the Nittany Lions one spot higher than their placement on the preseason AP Poll .

Considering they are behind four Big Ten teams — Oregon , Ohio State , Indiana , and Michigan — the index only gives Penn State a 4.6% chance of winning the conference. But luckily, you don't have to be the best team in the nation or win your conference to advance to the College Football Playoff, which is why they have a 22.8% chance to make it.

These numbers will change a lot over the course of the season, but this is far from a bad starting point for the Nittany Lions . They don't get their first real test until Week 4 against Wisconsin , so they could surge up the list if some the teams ahead of them hit some road bumps early on. Let's see just how high they can get before the big tests in the middle of the season against Michigan and USC .

articles.title: American Folarin Balogun’s Everton Move Collapses After Failed Medical
articles.summary: What looked like one of the more straightforward deals of deadline day has dramatically unraveled. Folarin Balogun’s proposed transfer from AS Monaco to Ever...
articles.body:
What looked like one of the more straightforward deals of deadline day has dramatically unraveled. Folarin Balogun's proposed transfer from AS Monaco to Everton is now in serious jeopardy after the American striker reportedly failed his medical with the Premier League club.

A Deal That Depended on Ndiaye's Exit First

Everton had agreed a fee with Monaco reported in the $54-58 million (£40-43 million) range, with Fabrizio Romano pegging the figure at $58 million (£42.8 million), and personal terms were already in place with the 25-year-old on a four-year contract. Crucially, the move only became possible once Everton completed a separate deal sending Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City for $88 million (£65 million) — Ndiaye had already passed his own medical ahead of that transfer, clearing the financial room for Everton to move on Balogun. Everton had also beaten out competition from both Aston Villa and Barcelona to reach an agreement with Monaco in the first place. Instead of completing the formalities, Everton's medical staff raised concerns that the forward isn't currently 100% fit.

Monaco and Balogun's Camp Push Back Hard

Monaco and Balogun's representatives strongly dispute the assessment. Both sides insist the former Arsenal academy product is ready to play and that there's no underlying issue that should block the move. RMC Sport reported that the move "now seems very unlikely, unless there's a last-minute change of heart," leaving the transfer hanging by a thread with England's window set to close at 11 p.m. BST.

Balogun hasn't featured for Monaco this season after picking up what the club described as a minor injury during World Cup duty with the United States. He returned late to preseason and only recently rejoined full group training, a history that appears to have factored heavily into Everton's caution during the medical process at Finch Farm. In 91 appearances for Monaco, Balogun has scored 31 goals, and he added three more in four appearances for the U.S. at this summer's World Cup.

The collapse, if confirmed, is a real blow for David Moyes's side. Everton had already sent Beto to Fiorentina partly to clear the path for Balogun's arrival and were counting on the striker to bolster a thin group of attacking options — a need made even sharper now that Ndiaye is gone to Manchester City as well.

As of this writing, the deal isn't officially dead, but multiple French and English outlets describe it as highly unlikely to be salvaged unless Everton's medical department has a sudden change of heart before the deadline. For Balogun, a return to the Premier League — the league where his career began — looked like the ideal next step after a strong World Cup and a productive season in Ligue 1. Instead, he now faces the real possibility of staying at Monaco until at least January, when the transfer window reopens and this opportunity could resurface.

articles.title: Rams owner Stan Kroenke agrees to buy the Angels; record $4 billion valuation
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams owner Stan Kroenke has reached an agreement to buy the Angels, ending the tenure of longtime owner Arte Moreno.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams owner Stan Kroenke has reached an agreement to buy the Angels, ending the tenure of longtime owner Arte Moreno.

The deal was made through Kroenke Sports and Entertainment (KSE), Kroenke's holding company.

The Angels were sold for a valuation of $4 billion, sources told ESPN's Buster Olney, beating the previous MLB record for a sale of $3.9 billion set by the Padres' new owner earlier this year.

"The Angels are a storied franchise anchored in a great market. We look forward to an exciting future with the Angels organization" Kroenke said in a press releasing announcing the deal.

The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, and needs to be approved by Major League Baseball. Details about the sale and the terms were not immediately available.

KSE now owns a team in all four of the major North American sports: The NFL's Rams, NBA's Nuggets, NHL's Avalanche and now the Angels. Kroenke also owns Arsenal of the English Premier League. The Rams, Nuggets, Avalanche and Arsenal have all won a championship in their sport over the last decade.

"The Moreno Family has been honored to steward the Angels for 23 years and we believe with KSE's experience and success they are the best next owner for the franchise," Moreno said in a statement. "The Angels Organization looks forward to continuing its commitment to the fans, our employees, the players and our business partners."

The Angels have struggled through much of Moreno's tenure as owner since he acquired the team in 2003 and have not had a postseason appearance since 2014. Fans have been calling for Moreno to sell the Angels.

"I started crying. I'm not gonna lie. I got a little teary eyed. I mean there's been so much leading up to this moment, and we put in a lot of work," said Angels fan Jonny Gonzalez, who created an Instagram page named Angels Boycott and was part of fan protests this season.

"The fans have put in a lot of the work and the atmosphere this year at the stadium has been different," Gonzalez said. "The crowd, the fans have been different this year as well and we're just happy that it finally paid off."

Other fans who spoke with Eyewitness News say they are not only thrilled by the sale but by who made the purchase.

Fans say they believe Kroenke's record speaks for itself and are encouraged by the success of the other franchises he owns.

articles.title: OKC Thunder Mailbag: How healthy is roster heading into 2026-27 training camp?
articles.summary: Oklahoma City Thunder Mailbag: How healthy is roster heading into 2026-27 training camp?
articles.body:
As the calendar flips to September, we're officially in the quiet zone of the NBA year. Not much will go on until the final days of the month. All of the major offseason moves have already happened. Teams across the league enjoy some serenity before the marathon starts back up again.

The Oklahoma City Thunder will enter the 2026-27 season as co-title favorites — alongside the San Antonio Spurs . Even with their offseason departures, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren should keep them in the middle of the title hunt.

With nothing else happening, Thunder Wire will regularly conduct Thunder Mailbags over the remainder of the offseason. In this edition, a social media user asked about the health status of some notable players. Of course, injuries have plagued OKC for the last two years.

In one season, it didn't matter. Even with Holmgren missing three months with a hip fracture, the Thunder went on to win the 2025 NBA championship. The bill came due eventually, though. That's what happened in the other season. By the end of OKC's 2026 playoff run, Williams' and Ajay Mitchell's absences were too much to overcome. They eventually fell in a 2026 Western Conference Finals Game 7 loss.

Now, how are Williams, Mitchell and Thomas Sorber doing? All three ended last season in street clothes. Williams sustained four hamstring strains in five months. The constant soft-tissue setbacks forced him to miss most of OKC's postseason run. Mitchell missed OKC's last four games with a soleus strain. And Sorber missed the whole 2025-26 season with a torn ACL he sustained in Sept. 2025.

I expect all three to be at OKC's training camp — which usually starts in the final days of September or the start of October. Williams has spent time with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's NBA trainer this offseason. Likely with the hope that he can overcome any chronic hamstring problems he battled through last year. But there's zero reason to believe those concerns should translate over to this upcoming season. Especially since four months will have passed.

It's easier to let your hamstring injuries heal in the summer — without the constant pressure of rushing back to help the Thunder get wins. For whatever reason, Williams just couldn't get over those problems. It was constant start-stop-start-stop once the 2026 New Year rolled around.

Same with Mitchell. It took him until July to fully rehab his season-ending soleus strain — which shows he would've missed the entire 2026 NBA Finals had OKC advanced to face the New York Knicks . But now, a couple of months later, he's back in the gym and logging his offseason work.

And then there's Sorber. He hasn't played a competitive game since Feb. 2015. That's a long time. By the time the preseason rolls around in Oct. 2026, 18 months will have passed. He had a follow-up procedure on his surgically-repaired knee in June 2026. Only expected to miss a month, he was likely cleared in Aug. 2026 to return to action. Giving him plenty of time to get ready for OKC's training camp.

We'll see if the Thunder can enjoy some better health luck. They're more than due in that department. Amazing that Gilgeous-Alexander, Williams and Holmgren haven't had a relatively-healthy year together since the 2023-24 season.

articles.title: Seton Hall basketball adds Israeli big as roster nearly finalized
articles.summary: 3 things to know about Seton Hall's latest roster addition and the state of the 2026-27 roster
articles.body:
Seton Hall basketball has mined the international pipeline here and there over the years. Now, for the first time, that pipeline has extended to Israel.

Ilay Dolinski, who grew up in Tel Aviv, has joined the Pirates' 2026-27 roster right at the start of the fall semester.

Here are three things to know about the 6-foot-9 forward.

1. He has extensive international experience.

Dolinski, who will turn 22 in February, played for Israel's senior national team in the 2026 FIBA World Cup. Over four games he averaged 4.3 points, 2.3 rebounds and 2.5 fouls in 12 minutes, shooting 7-of-17 from the field, 2-of-6 from 3-point range, and 1-of-3 from the free-throw line.

He also played professionally for Kiryat in Israel's Winner League, that county's highest level of pro hoops, appearing in 20 games during the 2025-26 campaign and averaging 7.7 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.2 assists, 0.9 blocks, 2.8 fouls and 1.9 turnovers in 17 minutes. He shot 49 percent from 2-point range, 25 percent from 3-point range (8-of-32) and 75 percent from the free-throw line (27-of-36).

Though he's listed as a center in some places and no weight is available (as is often the case with internationals), Dolinski doesn't appear to have the frame of a Big East center and likely will factor as more of a power forward.

On July 22 Draft Express's Jonathan Givony announced that Dolinski had committed to Tulsa, citing agent Misko Raznatovic as the source. However, he never turned up on Tulsa's 2026-27 roster as listed on the program's website. You know who is listed there, though? Mike Williams, who averaged 7.0 points as a mercurial starting guard for Seton Hall last winter.

Consider it a trade of sorts: Early last offseason, Williams had arrived at an agreement with the Hall's staff to return to the Pirates for this season, only to renege and relocate.

The bottom line: In 2026 commitment announcements should be taken with a grain of salt (the Pirates lost two commits already this offseason). When a player arrives on campus and is practicing with the team, that's how you know he's committed. Dolinksi arrived in South Orange this week and has begun working out on campus.

Dolinski is among a handful of incoming Pirates who hail from another country. This mirrors a sport-wide trend in search of better value and marks the first time Shaheen Holloway has mined this route to a significant extent. As has been reported, Seton Hall is also zeroing in on adding Theo Airhienbuwa, a 6-foot-7 wing from Italy, to round out the roster before fall semester add/drop ends Sept. 8.

If the foreign pipeline works out this coming season, and assuming the NCAA continues to lax eligibility standards for foreign pros, expect it to become a regular feature of the Hall's recruiting going forward.

Seton Hall's projected 2026-27 depth chart

Guards (7): Del Jones, Simeon Wilcher, Trey Parker, Kareem Thomas, Roddie Anderson, Mihailo Petrovic, Darien 'Payday' Moore.

Bigs (4) : Terry Copeland, Devin Williams, Ilay Dolinski, Abdulai Fanta Kabba.
